chunks.full_text: Number Formats: Binary Number System Thebinary number systemis abase-2 numeral systemthat uses only two digits: 0 and 1. Regardless of size, every number can be represented in binary form, making it the fundamental numbering system for computers and digital systems. Examples:•14 in binary:11102•245 in binary:111101012•34567 in binary:10000111000011112 All data in a computer is stored in binary, whether it's text, images, or numbers.Why Binary?Computers use binary because they operate using electrical signals with two states: ON (1) and OFF (0). This makes binary the most efficient way to represent and process data electronically.Memory consists of individual bits (binary digits), each of which is either a 0 or 1. These bits are grouped into bytes (8 bits), and sequences of bytes are used to store more complex data, such as numbers, characters, or larger structures like arrays and files.

chunks.full_text: Why are Integers popular in coding?§Efficiency: Integers are stored and processed more quickly by the CPU compared to floating-point numbers.§Exact Values: Unlike floating-point numbers, integers represent exact values without rounding errors.§Memory Usage: Integers require less memory compared to more complex data types like floats or doubles.§Looping and Indexing: Commonly used to control loops and index arrays due to their precision and simplicity.§Bitwise Operations: Integers are ideal for bit-level operations (AND, OR, XOR) and shifting, commonly used in low-level programming.§Compatibility: Widely supported by all programming languages and hardware architectures.

Power Set The power set of a set is the set of all possible subsets of that set, including the empty set and the set itself. If S is a set, the power set of S is usually denoted as P(S) or 2S.Example:For the set S={a,b}, the power set P(S) is: P(S)={∅,{a},{b},{a,b}} Cardinality of Power Set: The number of elements in the power set of S is 2n, where n is the number of elements in S. For example, |P(S)|=22=4

chunks.full_text: Cartesian Product The Cartesian product of two sets is the set of all ordered pairs where the first element in each pair is from the first set, and the second element is from the second set. The Cartesian product of sets A and B is denoted as A×B.Example:A={1,2} and B={a,b}; A×B={(1,a),(1,b),(2,a),(2,b)}Order Matters! The order of sets in a Cartesian product is significant. A×B is not necessarily the same as B×A. For instance, using the sets from the above example, B×A={(a,1),(a,2),(b,1),(b,2)}, which is different from A×B.

Decimal Number System.text: Number Formats: Decimal Number System Thedecimal number system(base-10) is the standard system for representing numbers, using the digits 0 through 9. Each position in a decimal number has aplace valuebased on powers of 10, making it intuitive for everyday use.Base-10: The decimal system uses10 digits(0–9).Place Value: Each digit's position determines its value, increasing by powers of 10 as you move left.Example:The number3471represents:3×103=30004×102=4007×101=701×100=1Total:3000+400+70+1=3471

Binary Number System.text: Number Formats: Binary Number System Thebinary number systemis abase-2 numeral systemthat uses only two digits: 0 and 1. Regardless of size, every number can be represented in binary form, making it the fundamental numbering system for computers and digital systems. Examples:•14 in binary:11102•245 in binary:111101012•34567 in binary:10000111000011112 All data in a computer is stored in binary, whether it's text, images, or numbers.Why Binary?Computers use binary because they operate using electrical signals with two states: ON (1) and OFF (0). This makes binary the most efficient way to represent and process data electronically.Memory consists of individual bits (binary digits), each of which is either a 0 or 1. These bits are grouped into bytes (8 bits), and sequences of bytes are used to store more complex data, such as numbers, characters, or larger structures like arrays and files.

Binary Number System and Modular Arithmetic Thebinary number system(base-2) andmodular arithmeticare closely related. Modular arithmetic operates on numbers with a fixed range, much like how binary numbers wrap around when adding or subtracting (mod2).

Arithmetic Sequence.text: Arithmetic Sequence An arithmetic sequence (progression) is a sequence of numbers in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant. This difference is called the "common difference," denoted by d. The general form of an arithmetic sequence is a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d, …, here, a is the first term of the sequence.The nth term of an arithmetic sequence can be calculated using the formula: an=a+(n−1)d Example:In the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …, the common difference d is 3.

Geometric Sequence.text: Geometric Sequence•A geometric sequence (progression) is a sequence of numbers where each term after the first is found by multiplying the previous term by a fixed, non-zero number called the "common ratio," denoted by r. The general form of a geometric sequence is: a, ar, ar2, ar3,…, here, a is the first term of the sequence.The nth term of a geometric sequence can be calculated using the formula: an=a⋅r(n−1) Example:In the sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, … the common ratio r is 2.

Subset.text: Subsets A set A is considered a (weak) subset of set B if every element of set A is also an element of set B. The notation used to represent this relationship is A⊆B, which can be read as "A is a subset of B”.This is analogous to the relation “less or equal.”The empty set ∅ is a subset of every set.Examples:•If A={1,2} and B={1,2,3,4}, then A⊆B, because every element of set A (which are 1 and 2) is also an element of set B. •If C={1,2,3,4}, then C⊆B, also C = B.

Subset.text: Proper Subset If A is a subset of B, and A is not equal to B (meaning some element in B is not in A), then A is called a proper subset of B. The notation used for a proper subset is A⊂B.This is analogous to the relation “less”.Examples:•If A={a,b} and B={a,b,c,d,e}, then A⊂B because A is a subset of B, and there exist the elements in B (which are c, d, e) that are not in A. If C={a,b,c,d,e}, it is NOT a proper subset of B.•Remember, by this definition, every set is considered a subset of itself (A⊆A) since all elements of A are indeed in A. However, a set is not a proper subset of itself.

Ordered Pair.text: Cartesian Product The Cartesian product of two sets is the set of all ordered pairs where the first element in each pair is from the first set, and the second element is from the second set. The Cartesian product of sets A and B is denoted as A×B.Example:A={1,2} and B={a,b}; A×B={(1,a),(1,b),(2,a),(2,b)}Order Matters! The order of sets in a Cartesian product is significant. A×B is not necessarily the same as B×A. For instance, using the sets from the above example, B×A={(a,1),(a,2),(b,1),(b,2)}, which is different from A×B.

Power Set.text: Power Set The power set of a set is the set of all possible subsets of that set, including the empty set and the set itself. If S is a set, the power set of S is usually denoted as P(S) or 2S.Example:For the set S={a,b}, the power set P(S) is: P(S)={∅,{a},{b},{a,b}} Cardinality of Power Set: The number of elements in the power set of S is 2n, where n is the number of elements in S. For example, |P(S)|=22=4
Power Set.example: For the set S={a,b}, the power set P(S) is: P(S)={∅,{a},{b},{a,b}}

Power Set.text: Example: Power Set S={p,q,r,s}The power set P(S) is the set of all possible subsets of S, including the empty set and S itself.P(S)={∅,{p},{q},{r},{s},{p,q},{p,r},{p,s},{q,r},{q,s},{r,s},{p,q,r}, {p,q,s},{p,r,s},{q,r,s},{p,q,r,s}} There are a total of 24=16 subsets in the power set P(S)

Cartesian Product Of Sets.text: Cartesian Product The Cartesian product of two sets is the set of all ordered pairs where the first element in each pair is from the first set, and the second element is from the second set. The Cartesian product of sets A and B is denoted as A×B.Example:A={1,2} and B={a,b}; A×B={(1,a),(1,b),(2,a),(2,b)}Order Matters! The order of sets in a Cartesian product is significant. A×B is not necessarily the same as B×A. For instance, using the sets from the above example, B×A={(a,1),(a,2),(b,1),(b,2)}, which is different from A×B.

Interval.text: What are Intervals?Intervals are a subset of the real number line, usually referring to all numbers between two endpoints. The nature of the inclusion of these endpoints defines different types of intervals.Interval Type Definition Description Open Interval(a,b)Contains all numbers between a and b but not including a and b.Closed Interval[a,b]Contains all numbers between a and b including a and b.Half-Open Interval (Left)(a,b]Contains all numbers between a and b, including b but excluding a.Half-Open Interval (Right)[a,b)Contains all numbers between a and b, including a but excluding b.Infinite Interval (Right)(a,∞)Contains all numbers greater than a.Infinite Interval (Left)(−∞,a)Contains all numbers less than a.Closed Infinite (Right)[a,∞)Contains all numbers greater than or equal to a.Closed Infinite (Left)(−∞,a]Contains all numbers less than or equal to a.
